# Tako

> Tako is a data intelligence platform. The Tako MCP server lets AI agents search a proprietary, continuously-updated knowledge base of 100K+ curated charts — carrying the latest reported quarter, same-day market prices, and official releases as they publish, not static historical reference — get grounded answers, explore Tako's data graph, fetch underlying source content, and run a multi-step Answer Agent. It is a hosted remote MCP server on Cloudflare Workers.

## Documentation

- [MCP Server Setup](https://github.com/TakoData/tako-mcp): Connect to the hosted Tako MCP server
- [API Reference](https://tako.com/docs/): Full REST API documentation
- [Chart Gallery](https://tako.com/gallery): Browse example charts and visualizations
- [OpenAPI Spec](https://tako.com/openapi.yaml): Machine-readable API specification

## Connecting

Hosted endpoint: `https://mcp.tako.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP). The ChatGPT app uses its own OAuth-only surface at `https://mcp.tako.com/mcp/chatgpt`.

- No token needed: paste the URL and sign in when the client prompts — a per-host key is minted automatically, and a new account gets up to 2,000 free requests. Anonymous connections work immediately: `tako_search` and `tako_available_data` run (rate-limited, shared capacity); `tako_contents` stays listed and answers with sign-in instructions when called.
- CI, headless runs, and clients without an OAuth flow: pass `Authorization: Bearer <TAKO_API_KEY>` on the same URL. Get a key at tako.com/console/api-keys.

Choosing tools: `?tools=` on the endpoint URL is an ALLOWLIST that REPLACES the default listing, so name every tool you want in one comma-separated list. Tokens are tool names with the `tako_` prefix optional, e.g. `https://mcp.tako.com/mcp?tools=search,available_data,contents,agent`. Listed by default: `tako_search`, `tako_available_data`, `tako_contents`, `tako_graph_related`. Opt-in, so reachable only by naming them: `tako_answer` (not recommended: the calling model already synthesizes from search results), `tako_agent` (the multi-step Answer Agent), `tako_visualize` (listed by default on `/mcp/chatgpt`, the surface whose host renders its chart widget inline). Unknown tokens are ignored, and a param that names nothing recognizable serves the defaults, so a typo never breaks the connection. `/mcp/chatgpt` ignores the param: its listing is fixed at submission.

Tools are discovered at runtime via `tools/list`. There is no per-call `api_token` argument — auth is connection-level.

## Available Tools

### Getting values vs. getting pointers

`tako_search` serves both jobs — the switch is `include_contents`:

- **Recon and fan-outs** (the default, `include_contents: false`): cards carry headline values, node ids, and chart links. Cheap; fire many narrow one-entity+one-metric queries in parallel and assemble the result yourself. The top card auto-renders inline as a chart.
- **The values themselves** (`include_contents: true`): the same cards with each exportable card's most-recent rows inlined (billed per 1k rows).
- **The full series or a page's text**: `tako_contents` on the result's url.

Never send a broad or multi-part question as one call — split it into narrow entity+metric searches (e.g. "US CPI inflation", "US core CPI inflation", "US PCE inflation", "US core PCE inflation"). For open-ended, multi-step research use `tako_agent` (opt-in).

### tako_search
Reconnaissance and chart retrieval across Tako's data graph and the live web, returned as structured `cards` plus `web_results`; the top card auto-renders inline as a chart (interactive widget on the ChatGPT app surface, chart image elsewhere). Set `include_contents: true` when you need the values — it inlines each exportable card's most-recent rows (billed per 1k rows); left false (the default), cards still carry headline values and chart links, right for breadth (many narrow queries fanned out in parallel to see what exists), for a chart when the embed is the deliverable, and to harvest node ids and urls.

Built to fan out: each query should resolve one entity + one metric ("Apple revenue", "Nvidia vs AMD gross margin"), and many narrow queries fired in parallel retrieve far better than one broad or compound query. To see what proprietary data exists — or confirm a specific figure exists before you spend a query — check `tako_available_data` first (free). Ground a query by pinning resolved graph ids. For a card's full rows call `tako_contents` — only when the card is marked `exportable: true`. A non-exportable card (`exportable: false`, usually license-gated) carries no rows on any path: read its headline value from the card's `description` when it carries one (each such card carries a `values_hint` saying exactly this). Repeated source/methodology paragraphs are hoisted out of the cards into the trailing Source Notes section of the markdown, keyed by source name — look a card's `source_name` up there (truncating clients lose boilerplate before data). For open-ended research use `tako_agent` (opt-in). Results arrive as a markdown document — a Tako Data section (per card: headline, exportable flag, node ids, chart link, a rows-count pointer), then Web Results, then Source Notes; the cards' actual rows and the web results' snippets ride in structuredContent (`cards[].content`, `web_results[].snippet`), not the markdown, alongside machine essentials (usage, chart-widget fields).

Parameters:
- `query` (string, required): Natural-language query — one entity + one metric; parallelize multiple.
- `sources` (array): both by default (`["data","web"]`) — keep web enabled. Only narrow to `["data"]` once `tako_available_data` has confirmed the proprietary data exists; otherwise web is the fallback when it does not. Pass `["web"]` for live web only. (`"tako"` is a legacy synonym for `"data"`.)
- `effort` (string, "fast" | "instant"): "fast" (default) or "instant" (fastest, cached embeds). Omit for fast.
- `count` (integer, 1-20, default 10): Maximum results per source.
- `include_contents` (boolean, default false): Set true to inline each exportable card's most-recent rows (billed per 1k rows) — do this when you need the values themselves. Left false, cards carry headline values and chart links. Requires a signed-in connection; anonymous calls that set it are refused with sign-in instructions. Full exports are a separate `tako_contents` call.
- `preview_rows` (integer, 1-250, default 20): Cap on each card's inlined MOST-RECENT rows when `include_contents` is true; lower it to trim context and spend on broad fan-outs. For more rows call `tako_contents` (max_rows up to 2,000, billed per 1k rows). Ignored when `include_contents` is false.
- `country_code` (string, default "US"): ISO country code.
- `locale` (string, default "en-US"): Locale.
- `node_ids` (array of strings, max 20, optional): Graph node ids (from `tako_available_data`, or a card's `nodes`) to PIN into the proprietary data source — strong retrieval boost.
- `strict` (boolean, default false): Hard filter — when true, return ONLY cards matching at least one pinned node (requires non-empty `node_ids`).

### tako_answer
Opt-in tool — off by default; enable with `?tools=answer` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting). Not recommended: the calling model already synthesizes from `tako_search` results, so a prose-answer tool is double synthesis. When enabled: ask one specific, self-contained data question and get one synthesized answer grounded in the `cards` it cites. What it adds over retrieval: it reads cited pages internally so their content shapes the answer without a second call, auto-renders the top cited card inline as a chart, and returns a coverage verdict. Rows are NOT included unless you set `include_contents: true`, and they bill per 1k when you do — cited cards otherwise carry a rows-count pointer in the prose, not the rows. When zero data cards ground the answer, a `guidance` field states the coverage miss deterministically (pivot; don't rephrase-retry). Also the values channel for non-exportable cards: when a search card is `exportable: false` (usually license-gated), ask here with that card's METRIC node id ALONE (the `mt::` entry in its `nodes`) pinned and `strict: true` to get the figures — pinning every node id on the card, or omitting strict, does not steer retrieval. Like `tako_search`, shared source/methodology paragraphs ride once in the trailing Source Notes section keyed by source name instead of repeating per card. For breadth or a chart card instead of a figure, use `tako_search` (parallelized into narrow entity+metric queries); when the question is what Tako covers, use `tako_available_data`. To pull a cited card's full rows, call `tako_contents` on its url (only when it's marked `exportable: true`). Results arrive as markdown — the synthesized answer first, then cited data cards (with a rows-count pointer, not the rows) and web citations, then Source Notes; the cited cards' actual rows ride in structuredContent (`cards[].content`), not the markdown, alongside machine essentials (usage, guidance).

Parameters:
- `query` (string, required): One specific, self-contained question.
- `sources` (array, optional): both by default (`["data","web"]`) — keep web enabled. Only narrow to `["data"]` once `tako_available_data` has confirmed the proprietary data exists; otherwise web is the fallback when it does not. Pass `["web"]` for live web only. (`"tako"` is a legacy synonym for `"data"`.)
- `include_contents` (boolean, default false): Set true to inline each cited data card's recent rows alongside the answer (billed per 1k rows); left false, the response is prose + citations only. Cited web pages are never auto-inlined.
- `preview_rows` (integer, 1-250, default 20): Cap on each cited card's inlined MOST-RECENT rows when `include_contents` is true (billed per 1k rows). Ignored when it is false.
- `country_code` (string, default "US"): ISO country code.
- `locale` (string, default "en-US"): Locale.
- `node_ids` (array of strings, max 20, optional): Graph node ids to PIN into the proprietary data source — strong retrieval boost.
- `strict` (boolean, default false): Hard filter — when true, return ONLY cards matching at least one pinned node (requires non-empty `node_ids`).

### tako_contents
Fetch the real content behind result URLs (1-10 per call) from `tako_search` — the rows behind a Tako card (CSV by default, or JSON), or a web page's full text. Requires a signed-in connection; anonymous calls return sign-in instructions. It is the step after search when you need the full data to compute over or quote. Batch them: fetching 8 pages in one call costs the same as 8 calls but saves 7 round trips, and every extra round trip re-sends the whole conversation as input tokens.

Precondition (Tako cards): non-exportable cards (`exportable: false`, usually license-gated) always 403 — never call this on them; their headline value is in the card's `description` (when present; see the card's `values_hint`). Call only on `exportable: true` cards, and even then a rare card still 403s: read the headline instead, don't retry. Web URLs always work.

Parameters:
- `urls` (array of string, 1-10, required): The result URLs to fetch — Tako card `webpage_url`s, web-result URLs, or a mix. Each is fetched and BILLED independently and one URL failing does not fail the others (its entry carries an `error` instead of a payload). Results are returned in `results`, positionally aligned with the URLs you passed.
- `url` (string, optional): Deprecated single-URL form, equivalent to `urls: [url]`. Prefer `urls`.
- `content_format` (string, optional): Tako cards only — serialization of the data: `csv` (default, text in `data`), `json_records` (row objects in `records`), or `json_compact` (compact columns+rows in `dataset`). Ignored for web URLs (always text).
- `max_rows` (integer, 1-2000, optional): Tako cards only — max rows to return (billed per 1k rows). Omit for the 20-row default; raise up to 2,000 for a larger export. Ignored for web URLs (use `max_chars`).
- `max_chars` (integer, 1-1,000,000, optional): Web URLs only — character cap on the extracted page text (1,000,000 = full text). Inline fetches default to 100,000; billing is per page regardless, so the cap only trims what reaches you (`truncated: true` reports a cut). Raise it toward 1,000,000 for a full long document inline. In url mode the downloaded file is the full text unless you set this (an explicit value caps the file too). Ignored when `query` is set (passages always scan the full text) and for Tako card URLs (use `max_rows`).
- `query` (string, optional): Web URLs + inline mode only — return just the passages around case-insensitive matches of this query (full phrase first, per-word fallback) instead of the full page text; one call lands on the relevant section of a long page, and the full text is always scanned regardless of `max_chars`. The `note` field summarizes the matches; a no-match note says so explicitly (a deterministic miss — try another url, not another wording). Ignored for Tako card URLs and in url mode.
- `mode` (string, "inline" | "url", default "inline"): Delivery only, not row count — `inline` returns the data in the response so you can read it; `url` returns a short-lived presigned `download_url` to the same file.

### tako_available_data
Find what proprietary, continuously-updated structured data exists on something — summarized in one call. Free and fast. Ask it when the question IS coverage: what does Tako have on X, is this measure tracked at all, what is it called — then build the real question around what comes back. Worth one call when you need a measure's EXACT name, since resolving it to the canonical form measurably improves what the priced call retrieves. Works on an entity (a company, person, or place → the metrics tracked on it, e.g. Tesla) or a metric (→ the entities it is tracked across, e.g. Inflation Rate), reported as a natural-language summary you can show the user.

Two paths, chosen by whether you pass `metric`:
- **Lookup** (`q` + `metric`, e.g. `q="Carnival", metric="passenger cruise days"`) — resolves the entity+metric PAIR directly in ~0.6s and returns a runnable `next_call`. Use it whenever you already know the measure.
- **Discovery** (`q` alone) — lists what the resolved node covers, for browsing. Candidate names are relevance-gated against `q` (name matches rank above alias matches), so a fuzzy graph hit about a different company is not reported as coverage.

The exact metric/entity names are the terms to reuse in the follow-up call; `structuredContent.matches[].coverage.items[]` pairs each name with its `node_id`. To land on exactly one metric, pin THAT metric node id alone with `strict: true` and name the entity in the query text — an entity-only pin, or a pin without `strict`, is a measured no-op. When the measure is known, `next_call` is that follow-up prewritten (query + the metric node + `strict`) — run it verbatim.

A broad entity's coverage list is capped and may be truncated: treat a name you don't see as UNCONFIRMED rather than absent. This tool confirms a name EXISTS in the graph; it cannot confirm a chart exists behind it — the `next_call` is that check, and if it comes back with 0 cards, run the same query once more with `node_ids` removed before concluding Tako has no data: the pin is a hard filter and the data is often held under a sibling metric node. `found: false` is a real answer: report the gap rather than silently falling back to web.

Parameters:
- `q` (string, required, min 2 chars): The NAME of the entity (or metric) to look up. Put the measure in `metric`, not here.
- `metric` (string, optional, min 2 chars): The measure you want, when you already know it — e.g. "gross margin", "capex". Supplying it selects the fast lookup path above.
- `types` (string, "entity" | "metric", optional): Narrow resolution to a thing ("entity") or a measure ("metric"); omit to search both.
- `label` (string, optional): NER label to prefer — a boost, not a filter. Supply it when you can categorize the term (company→ORG, country→GPE, person→PERSON, metric→METRIC, …). Describes the ENTITY only; it is not applied to `metric`.

### tako_graph_related
Listed by default. Explore what a graph node connects to — the map of what data Tako has for it. Free. Covers what `tako_available_data` does not: traversal relations (siblings, part_of, members, `rel:*` named edges like `rel:competes_with`), server-side `q` filtering within a relation, and cursor paging past the first page. Drilling `relation: "metrics"` returns only that node's metrics group — the smallest, cheapest view of its coverage; the overview (`node_id` alone) also returns entities, siblings, and named edges at more tokens. A listed metric is table-level evidence, not proof — `tako_search` is the final validator. Empty `items` is a normal answer: report the gap instead of silently falling back to web.

Parameters:
- `node_id` (string, required): Node id from `tako_available_data` or a card's `nodes`.
- `relation` (string, optional): Relation key to page — metrics, entities, siblings, part_of, members, or rel:<phrase>. Omit for the overview.
- `q` (string, optional): Case-insensitive substring filter on name+aliases — one string per call; for several name-variants of a metric ("revenue", "sales"), call once per variant.
- `label` (string, optional) / `infer_label` (boolean, optional): NER label to prefer when resolving — a boost, not a filter.
- `cursor` (string, optional) / `limit` (integer, 1-100, default 50): Pagination within a drilled relation.

### tako_visualize
Opt-in tool — name `visualize` in `?tools=` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting). Listed by default on the ChatGPT app surface (`/mcp/chatgpt`), which renders its chart inline as a widget; everywhere else enable it for the shareable embed URL. Create an embeddable Tako card from your OWN structured data (not from search), backed by Tako's Thin-Viz API. Provide one or more typed components; the card auto-renders inline as a chart and returns share/embed URLs.

Parameters:
- `components` (array, required): One or more `{ component_type, config, component_variant? }` objects. `component_type` is one of: header, generic_timeseries, categorical_bar, choropleth, data_table_chart, histogram, pie, table, financial_boxes, timeline, treemap, heatmap, marimekko, boxplot, waterfall, sankey, scatter, bubble, top_level_metric, person_card. `config` holds that type's data (validated server-side). The optional `component_variant` string selects a type variant (e.g. 'simple', 'financial'). `person_card` must be the only component.
- `title` (string, optional): Card title
- `description` (string, optional): Card description
- `source` (string, optional): Data source attribution shown in the footer
- `height` (integer, 100-2000, optional): Chart height in pixels
- `normalize_currencies` (string, optional): Target ISO 4217 code to convert currency-denominated datasets

### tako_agent
Opt-in tool — name `agent` in `?tools=` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting). Run Tako's Answer Agent for open-ended, multi-step questions whose shape needs figuring out — cohorts, ranking or filtering by criteria, aggregation, and multi-hop reasoning across many entities; also the fallback when `tako_search` / `tako_answer` return nothing. Returns a synthesized answer plus supporting chart cards (~30–90s). Not on the ChatGPT app surface (`/mcp/chatgpt`): that host sends no progressToken, so a polled run cannot stay inside its per-call timeout.

Parameters:
- `query` (string, required): The open-ended, analytical question.
- `sources` (array, optional): both by default (`["data","web"]`) — keep web enabled. Only narrow to `["data"]` once `tako_available_data` has confirmed the proprietary data exists; otherwise web is the fallback when it does not. Pass `["web"]` for open-web only. (`"tako"` is a legacy synonym for `"data"`.)
- `thread_id` (string UUID, optional): Continue a prior agent run's thread as a follow-up; omit to start a new thread.
